messages:
Alex: Hey — hitting repeated 401s when I try to call the inference API after swapping the project context. Repro steps: create SA in proj-alpha, mint JWT, exchange for access_token, then call /v1/gen with header `x-project: proj-beta` -> 401. Anyone seen this?
Marie: Can you paste the exchange/JWT payload? my guess is the audience/aud or sub is scoped to proj-alpha so token is rejected for proj-beta.
Alex: Paste below (sanitized):
```
{"iss":"service-account@proj-alpha.iam","sub":"service-account@proj-alpha.iam","aud":"https://auth.redwood-inference.internal/token","exp":...}
```
Alex: We do an HTTP POST to /token and get back access_token, expires_in, etc. Token looks valid but call is rejected.
Sam: Two likely causes: 1) routing requires the token to be minted for the target project (aud/sub tied to project), 2) client-side token cache is keyed only by SA key id and not by project header so the client reuses a token minted for proj-alpha when you switch headers.
Raj: +1 on caching. The Python SDK had a bug where token cache key was just `service_account_id` so multi-project callers hit this. Are you using the SDK or doing raw HTTP?
Alex: Raw HTTP, but we wrap it in a small client that caches tokens by SA key id. The system-level requirement I remember: token audience must be the token endpoint for the target project or include an `projects/*` claim. Is there a canonical rule?
Marie: For our OIDC/JWT flow: the token exchange requires `aud` to be the Redwood token endpoint (`https://auth.redwood-inference.internal/token`) but the service account's parent project must match the project you're routing the request to OR the token must include a `projects` claim that lists allowed projects. TL;DR: mint the token with the same project context or use a federated token that includes multiple projects.
Sam: Workarounds: 1) instantiate a client per project (cheap) so token cache is separate, 2) include `x-project` in the token cache key, 3) for short-term testing just mint token with `projects:["proj-beta"]`.
Alex: Example Python snippet that fixed it for me (caveat: simplified):
```
# ensure cache key includes project
def get_token(sa_key, project):
    cache_key = f"{sa_key['id']}:{project}"
    if cache.exists(cache_key):
        return cache.get(cache_key)
    token = exchange_jwt_for_token(sa_key, audience=TOKEN_URL, projects=[project])
    cache.set(cache_key, token, ttl=token['expires_in'] - 30)
    return token
```
Raj: Also watch streaming: the streaming websocket/HTTP2 connection binds to the access_token at connect time. If you swap projects mid-stream, you must reconnect with a new token. We had a production case where a long-lived stream kept using an old token and started getting 401s after a gradual policy change.
Marie: Retry guidance: do a single token-refresh + replay on 401 for idempotent requests. For non-idempotent stream ops, fail fast and reconnect. Avoid blind infinite retries — token refresh should be attempted once if you get a 401.
Alex: Good to know. Is there an SDK patch for the cache behavior?
DevEx Bot: Heads up — we merged a fix to the Python SDK earlier this week that keys token cache by (service_account_id, project). See internal doc: https://redwood.internal/devex/auth/service-accounts#multi-project-tokens (changes rolled in v0.11.3).
Sam: If anyone needs a backport for older releases, ping me and I can open a PR.
Alex: Thanks y'all, will try instantiating per-project client and/or patching our cache key.
Marie: If you still see failures after that, grab the `X-Request-Id` from the 401 response and post it here and we can trace in the gateway logs. :mag:
Alex: Will do — thanks! :thumbsup:
